title: HIV: Z21, B20 or R75
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's HIV status (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up on HIV management.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F, BMI 26.4.

Recent Labs: CD4 count: 650 cells/mm3; HIV viral load: Undetectable; eGFR: 88 mL/min/1.73m2.

Medication List:
- Biktarvy (dolutegravir/tenofovir alafamivir/emtricitabine)
- Multivitamin

Social History: The patient is a 51-year-old male who works as a software engineer. He lives with his spouse and a dog. He reports occasional social drinking and does not smoke.

Family History: Father had hypertension; Mother had Type 2 diabetes. No known family history of malignancy.

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Negative for fever, chills, or night sweats.
Respiratory: Negative for cough, shortness of breath, or wheezing.
Cardiovascular: Negative for chest pain or palpitations.
Gastrointestinal: Negative for nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea.
Genitourinary: Negative for dysuria or discharge.
Neurological: Negative for headaches or dizziness.
Musculoskeletal: Negative for joint pain or swelling.

HPI: Patient is a 51-year-old male with a known history of HIV. He was treated for Pneumocystis pneumonia several years ago. He is currently on a stable antiretroviral regimen. He reports feeling well overall and denies any acute respiratory symptoms or opportunistic infections.

Exam: General: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3. Constitutional: No acute distress. Skin: No rashes or lesions noted. HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. Respiratory: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Extremities: No edema.

Assessment: 
1. HIV: Stable on current antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load and healthy CD4 count.
2. History of Pneumocystis pneumonia: Resolved and stable.

Plan:
1. Continue current antiretroviral therapy as prescribed.
2. Continue routine monitoring of CD4 count and viral load every 6 months.
3. Patient instructed to report any new respiratory symptoms or fever immediately.
4. Return to clinic in 6 months for routine follow-up.

Electronically signed, 
J. Lindqvist, NP
May 14, 2026
explanations: Once a patient has had an HIV-related illness, B20 is used at every later encounter, even when well with an undetectable viral load.

distractors.why: A prior HIV-related illness means B20 from then on.
